title: Account Health Accelerator — 90m QBR Workshop Runbook & Facilitation Script
summary: Concise runbook for a 90-minute customer success QBR framed as a workshop to accelerate renewal readiness and create concrete next-step commitments. Emphasizes interactive diagnostics, prioritized risk triage, and a tailored renewal health scorecard.
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, reproducible runbook to run a 90-minute QBR framed as an interactive workshop — goal is to align on success outcomes, diagnose risk, and leave with prioritized actions tied to renewal readiness and measurable owners. Use for mid-to-large accounts where renewal is within 90–180 days or where adoption acceleration is a priority.

When to use this format:
- Renewal window 90–180 days and there are open risks or adoption gaps
- Need to create a prioritized action list with clear owners on the call
- Technical and product stakeholders should be present for live troubleshooting or unblock items

Participants (recommended):
- CSM (facilitator) — 1 (owner of the runbook)
- Customer Exec Sponsor — 1–2 (decision makers)
- Product/Technical Lead (customer) — 1–2
- Solutions Engineer / Customer Success Engineer — 1 (Redwood)
- Stakeholder from customer success ops or renewal team — optional

Pre-work (send 5 business days before):
- Short pre-read: 1 page summary with current usage, key incidents, health scorecard (attach)
- Ask customer to bring 2–3 success metrics they care about for the next 90 days
- Share list of data we will review (usage dashboard link, error logs, cost report)

Meeting logistics (90 minutes total):
- 00:00–00:05 — Welcome, purpose, and outcomes (CSM)
  - Quick context: "Today we want to confirm outcomes, identify top 3 risks, and leave with owners and deadlines."
- 00:05–00:20 — Current state snapshot (dashboard walkthrough) (CSM + Data)
  - Live screen: usage trends, latency/cost breakdown, incident timeline, feature adoption
  - Script cue: "I'll show 3 graphs — adoption, performance, and cost — call out any surprises we should pause on."
- 00:20–00:35 — Customer perspective & priorities (exec & product) (facilitated Q&A)
  - Prompt questions: "Given what you see, what's changed for your team since our last check-in? Which metric must move to consider this engagement successful?"
  - Capture verbatim customer outcome statements as commitments
- 00:35–00:55 — Risk triage & root-cause triage (working breakout or focused discussion)
  - Use risk ladder: High/Medium/Low + likelihood + impact
  - Live tool: create three risk cards on shared doc: Performance, Adoption, Integration/Support
  - Facilitation script: "For each risk, tell me the smallest experiment or fix that would materially reduce its impact."
- 00:55–01:10 — Action planning & owner assignment (prioritize top 3) (CSM + Customer)
  - Fill out action template inline: Action, Owner, Due date, Success criteria, Dependencies
  - Timebox discussions: 5–7 minutes per action
- 01:10–01:20 — Renewal readiness pulse & check (scorecard) (CSM)
  - Run a quick renewal readiness rubric (see below). Ask for a thumbs up/neutral/down from exec sponsor
- 01:20–01:30 — Close, decisions recap, and next steps (CSM)
  - Confirm meeting notes, who will send what, and date for 30-day checkpoint

Facilitation script (detailed cues):
- Opening (00:00–00:05): "Thanks everyone. Quick round-robin — name + role + one thing you want from today. I'll capture and we will try to surface or address each. At the end we should have 3 prioritized actions with owners and dates."
- Dashboard handoff (00:05–00:20): "I'll narrate the charts. Pause me whenever you want to deep-dive. Top three signals I'm watching are X, Y, Z — are those aligned with what you're seeing?"
- Customer perspective (00:20–00:35): "What does success look like in 90 days? If we could wave a wand and one metric moved, which one would it be?"
- Risk triage (00:35–00:55): "Let's name the top 3 risks. For each, we'll note: what's the immediate symptom, the likely root cause, and one small test/fix we can commit to in the next 2 weeks."
- Action planning (00:55–01:10): "We need actions that are specific and measurable. I'll propose a draft, you edit. Who owns it and by when? If there are blockers, name them now so we can scope the work."
- Renewal pulse (01:10–01:20): "I'll run a quick readiness rubric: Adoption (40%), Performance/Reliability (30%), Value Realization (20%), Contract/Org Alignment (10%). We'll score each area and produce an overall readiness rating and a short rationale."

Renewal readiness rubric (use quick scoring 1–5 per pillar):
- Adoption (40% weight): DAU/MAU for integrated flows, % of seats/modules activated
- Performance/Reliability (30% weight): incidents in last 90 days, p99 latency vs SLO
- Value Realization (20% weight): customer-reported outcomes achieved, ROI signal
- Contract/Org Alignment (10% weight): renewal decision maker engaged, budget signals

Scoring guide (example):
- 5 = On track, multiple success signals, low risk
- 3 = Mixed signals, mitigations needed
- 1 = Critical risk, immediate escalation recommended

Example output (what you should leave with):
- Top 3 risks + short root cause hypothesis
- Prioritized actions (3 max) with owners, dates, and success criteria
- Renewal readiness score: 3.2 / 5 (with short rationale)
- 30-day checkpoint date scheduled and owner for follow-up notes

Risk signals and mitigation playbook (cheat sheet):
- Adoption lag (signal: feature usage < 50% of expected): mitigate with tailored enablement session, quick product walkthrough, and success checklist for end users
- Performance regressions (signal: increased p99 latency or repeated GC spikes): mitigate with temporary routing to lower-latency model variant, escalate to SRE + providing logs and timeline
- Cost surprise (signal: unexpected token usage spike): mitigate with token budgeting, rate limiting suggestions, and Evaluate batching/quantization options through Optimize team

Action template (one-line per item):
- Action: [short description]
- Owner: [Name + email]
- Due date: [YYYY-MM-DD]
- Success criteria: [specific metric or outcome]
- Dependencies: [if any]

Post-meeting deliverables (CSM responsibilities within 48 hours):
- Send concise meeting notes with action table and owners
- Attach dashboard snapshot and annotated graphs used in the session
- Create follow-up Jira ticket(s) for technical work and link to action items
- Email renewal owner with readiness score and proposed renewal cadence

Escalation lanes (if readiness <= 2 or critical risk identified):
- Immediate: tag Head of CS and Solutions Engineering on Slack thread within 4 hours
- 24-hour: set up a technical deep-dive with SRE/Eng if performance is root cause
- 72-hour: prepare exec brief and proposed remediation budget if needed

Templates to copy into meeting doc (quick paste):
- "Outcomes we're targeting in 90 days:"
  - [Customer-stated outcome 1]
  - [Customer-stated outcome 2]
- "Top 3 risks (owner/hypothesis):"
  - Risk A — Owner — 1-line hypothesis
  - Risk B — Owner — 1-line hypothesis
- "Action table (copy):"
  - Action | Owner | Due | Criteria | Dependencies

Notes on tone and facilitation: keep it concise and collaborative. Avoid lengthy slide decks — prefer live data and interactive editing. If a contentious topic arises, park it into a follow-up 30–60 minute technical session rather than letting it consume the workshop.

Examples of sticky prompts to surface commitment: 
- "If we commit to this action, who will unblock the dependency?"
- "What's the smallest outcome that would materially change your renewal intent?"
- "If we could guarantee improved latency by X, would that change your usage plan?"

Follow-up cadence recommendations:
- 30-day short checkpoint (15–30m): review progress on top 3 actions
- 7-day tactical standup (optional) if there's a technical remediation in flight
- Final pre-renewal sync: 30 days before renewal decision (exec + CSM)

Appendix: quick checklist to run before the call
- [ ] Dashboard shared and pre-read sent 5 business days prior
- [ ] Exec sponsor confirmed attendance
- [ ] SE and product TL invited for technical items
- [ ] Action tracker template created in shared doc
- [ ] Required logs/reports attached to meeting invite

Appendix B: sample language for recording commitments in the notes (copy/paste):
- "Committed: Redwood to deliver A/B test of model routing to reduce p99 by 25% — Owner: Liam O'Connor — Due: 2025-12-10 — Success: p99 < target for 3 consecutive days."
- "Committed: Customer to enable feature X for pilot group of 50 users — Owner: Priya Shah (Customer) — Due: 2025-11-30 — Success: 70% activation among pilot cohort."

Usage guidance for CSMs:
- Timebox tightly. If technical debate exceeds 10 minutes, create a follow-up deep-dive and return to the workshop with a decision window.
- Prefer specific, measurable actions over vague "follow-ups." Use dates and owners.
- Keep the customer in the authorship role — ask them to state acceptance of the plan before leaving the call.

End of runbook.

- 2025-11-14: initial draft (Maya Patel)
- 2025-11-21: added escalation lanes and rubric weights (Diego Alvarez)
